# Discovery-prep brief: Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Privately held luxury hotel and resort company; majority shareholder is Cascade Investment, L.L.C. (about 71.25%), with Kingdom Holding Company (23.75%) and the Sharp family (5%). [1][2]
- Headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. [3]
- Operates about 135 hotels and resorts and 61 residential properties in 47 countries per its January 2026 65th-anniversary release; older references cite 133 hotels and resorts. [1][8][9][10][12]
- Reports nearly 60,000 colleagues; third-party trackers report lower figures (about 49,000 to 43,000). [5][6][7]
- Roughly 60 additional projects are in development, with 65% of the pipeline including a residential component. [8][9][10][11]
- No reliable public breakdown by region or property type was found, and source counts conflict. [8][11]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- Robert Fritz named Executive Chairman; Founder Isadore Sharp moves to Chairman Emeritus (date not stated in findings). [12][13]
- Berlin: Four Seasons agreed with Gruppo Statuto to take over management of Hotel de Rome; it operates as Hotel de Rome through 2026 and is to reopen as Four Seasons Hotel Berlin in 2027 after renovations (2025 press releases). [12][13][14]
- Sevilla, Spain: new hotel with Blasson announced, opening 2028 (2026). [14]
- Four Seasons Hotel Mykonos accepting reservations ahead of summer opening (May 2026). [1][12]
- Development update on October 20, 2026 covering 13 upcoming hotel and resort openings and reopenings across five regions, mostly 2027 and beyond. [8][11]
- Four Seasons Resort and Residences Puerto Rico opened November 2025; Venice Hotel Danieli is slated to reopen as a Four Seasons. [15]
- No reliable public reports found of financial or occupancy results, or sales or ownership changes, from October 2025 to October 2026. [1][12]

## What guests say (themes)

- Staff and spa facilities are the most praised aspects, with cleanliness and attentive service often commended, though lapses are mentioned. [16]
- Recurring complaint that service does not justify the premium price, with reviewers expecting a more elevated experience. [17]
- Check-in friction reported in more than one city (card declines in New York, a 20-minute check-in in Las Vegas). [18][19]
- Room and facility age and pool access are mixed points, including untouched bathrooms despite a 2020 renovation and pool waitlists. [17]

## Technology hints

- A 2000s-era announcement says OPERA Property Management System was selected for new properties; no current confirmation found. [20][21]
- A 2020 release describes a guest app for reservations and airport transfer requests via an on-call concierge. [21]
- A 2018 trade article says the chat service is staffed by people on property, not bots. [22]
- A 2018 CIO interview names Adobe for web and digital experience, and says the company uses Salesforce, Workday and Microsoft. [22][23]
- Vendor case studies (Medallia, Avero) claim Four Seasons uses their platforms; these are vendor marketing claims. [22][23][24]
- No booking engine or Preferred Partner platform details were found. [20]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which systems do you treat as the system of record for reservations, guest profiles, and folios today, and which of them are run by the corporate team versus each property?
2. How much of the property management stack is still OPERA, and which hotels, if any, run a different PMS?
3. Where does check-in actually slow down, and what share of arrivals hit the card-decline or long-wait problems seen in guest reviews?
4. How do guest feedback signals from Medallia reach property leaders, and how quickly do they lead to a changed action?
5. What does a service failure cost you today, and who measures whether the premium price is justified at each hotel?
6. Which parts of the Berlin and Sevilla openings or the 13-property pipeline depend on systems work, and who owns that work?
7. How are the AI conference-assistant and interpretation tools in Kuala Lumpur being measured, and what would make them roll out to other properties?
8. How do the AI waste-tracking tools at Papagayo feed into food and cost decisions, and who acts on the data?
9. Which operational tasks do property teams spend the most hours on that are still manual, such as reconciling data across Adobe, Salesforce, and the PMS?
10. Which of the systems named in 2018 and 2020 sources have been replaced since, and who in IT or operations could confirm the current stack?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Check-in and arrival friction reduction | Guest reviews report card declines and long check-ins in multiple cities, and the company has tested self check-in in Kuala Lumpur. [18][19][25] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Guest feedback triage and service recovery | Recurring reviews about service versus price suggest feedback is not tied quickly to action; Medallia is already in use, so a layer on top may fit. [17][22][23] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Kitchen food-waste analytics at buffet properties | A Four Seasons property already uses camera and scale tools for buffet waste, showing the cost problem is recognized. [27] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hello,
>
> I would like to learn how Four Seasons approaches guest-facing operations and the systems behind them. Would you be open to a 30-minute discovery call in the coming weeks? I would like to hear which processes take the most effort today and where the current tools fall short.
>
> If useful, I can send a few specific questions in advance so the time is well spent.
>
> Thank you,
> Vamsi
